failed_probe.hypothesis: Wide arrival spreads may justify a bounded market-entry wait for a narrower observed spread, but delay can worsen prices or miss valid entries. First establish whether this rule has enough actual quote interventions to merit a separately frozen financial comparison.

references.title: Understanding Order Types
references.scope: Stock order mechanics: market prices are uncertain; a limit price can prevent execution. This is not CFD strategy evidence.

references.title: Algorithmic Trading
references.scope: Adaptive and Arrival Price descriptions motivate an execution-cost/price-risk tradeoff. Our proposed spread-conditioned wait is neither an IBKR algo reproduction nor a demonstrated CFD improvement.

proposed_rules.baseline: Tick-count median of raw bid/ask spreads in [scheduled entry minus60s,scheduled entry); exclude current and all later quotes.
proposed_rules.trigger: If arrival spread exceeds the fixed baseline median, wait for the FIRST subsequent spread at or below it. Otherwise preserve arrival.
proposed_rules.execution: No resting limit, midpoint fill, assumed queue priority or price improvement. This audit only records quote times; a separate experiment must apply adverse market fills and every original guard at actual candidate time.
proposed_rules.cancellation: Sparse baseline is unavailable, not imputed. A waiting-path gap or deadline failure is retained. No new session eligibility, financial outcome or opportunity validity is inferred.

failed_probe.feasibility_gate: At least20 delayed_quote_candidate raw schedule events for EACH original lane, with complete frozen quote coverage and causal prefix parity. This does not establish20 executable trades.
failed_probe.no_tuning: If the gate fails, archive without alternate median windows, wait horizons, thresholds or sparse-data fallbacks. No later-history financial replay.
limitations: Previously exposed development prices are not untouched evidence.
